This occurs because 0.1 (which is 1/10 in decimal) cannot be expressed as a finite sum of negative powers of 2. Binary (base-2) systems only allow denominators that are powers of 2 (like 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, etc.), but 1/10 is not a power of 2. As a result, the binary representation of 0.1 is an infinite, repeating sequence, which cannot be stored exactly in finite computer memory, leading to rounding errors.
